title: Pager-wave handoff and long-tail metric gaps - scratchpad
content:
Context and purpose:

This scratchpad is a working record from the 2025-10-02 -> 2025-12-16 on-call rotation where we saw several pager waves driven by a combination of transient metric gaps and aggressive SLO burn alerts. The goal here is to capture the incident patterns, immediate triage steps we used, hypotheses that repeatedly showed up, and concrete runbook / alert-tuning proposals we should trial. This is intentionally rough — use for handoffs and follow-on tasks.

Summary of incidents observed:
- 2025-10-14 03:34 UTC: multi-service SLO burn alerts started for hosted inference paths; ~130 pages in 17m. Many alerts were identical: "SLO:99p latency breaches - route=generate-hosted" but digging into traces showed request throttling and missing downstream per-shard metrics.
- 2025-11-06 19:02 UTC: Prometheus scrape failures from the collector layer for ~6m caused derived error-rate alerts to spike. Pager wave, but most pages resolved when scrape resumed.
- 2025-12-10 11:11 UTC: synthetic test heartbeat missing for a subset of regions (eu-west1). This triggered both SLO and availability monitors.

Common patterns / signals that repeat:
- Metric-staleness (scrapes failing, flaky forwarder, collector OOM) looks like real incidents to SLO rules because we compute burn from derived counters.
- High-cardinality spikes from a deployment (a new model variant) temporarily increases metric cardinality and causes alert evaluation costs and grouping mismatches.
- Alerts with 0m "for" fire repeatedly when upstream metric briefly gaps, leading to immediate paging without human-evaluable context.
- Missing synthetic heartbeats cause cascading alerts across routing and dedicated pools.

Immediate triage checklist we used during waves (copy-paste runbook fragment):
1) Confirm scope: Query Grafana/Prometheus to see which metrics are missing. Example PromQL: absent_over_time(up{job=~"collector.*"}[5m]) or increase(requests_total[5m]) == 0 for endpoints.
2) Check ingestion pipeline: kafka-lag, forwarder logs (kafka-forwarder-*/stderr), and collector pods (kubectl -n observability get pods & logs).
3) Verify scrapes: grafana -> Explore -> top targets; check lastScrape, lastError.
4) Confirm SLO origin: find which derived metric feed into SLO. Use SLO mapping: confluence page (linked).
5) If metric gap is confirmed, mute SLO-derived alerts for the affected service via /alert-mute with a 30m window, note in #oncall.
6) Escalate only if underlying service shows live errors (5xx traces, increased latency, queue growth).

Evidence and queries we relied on (examples):
- Detecting metric staleness: 
  - PromQL: absent_over_time(scrape_series_added{job="prometheus"}[10m]) > 0
  - Or: (time() - max_over_time(timestamp(up{job=~"collector.*"})[15m])) > 300 -> flag stale
- SLO burn isolation: 
  - Grafana: panel using rate(error_count[1m]) / rate(request_count[1m]) by (route) to isolate which route contributes most.
- Cardinailty spike detection: topk(10, count by(model_variant) (increase(requests_total[5m]))) to find new high-cardinality keys.

Hypotheses (ranked):
A) Root cause: collector-side memory pressure + periodic GC stalls -> temporary drop of scrape targets. Evidence: collector pod OOMs correlated with missing metrics on 2025-11-06.
B) Root cause: deploys that introduce a new metric label (model_variant) causing high-cardinality and query timeouts, which in turn produces evaluation failures and false-positive alerts.
C) Root cause: overly sensitive SLO evaluation windows (0m "for") and SLO rules that don't account for partial data loss.

Short-term mitigations already tried (and outcome):
- Added a 5m mute recipe for SLO-derived pages to avoid immediate mass paging while we investigate. Outcome: reduced pages by ~80% during similar transient gaps but increased manual oversight required.
- Increased Prometheus remote write timeout on collectors from 20s -> 30s for a week. Outcome: reduced transient failures but did not eliminate them.
- Temp rule: require min_samples=3 in Grafana alert eval for derived metrics. Outcome: fewer false positives; some real incidents delayed.

Proposed medium-term runbook additions and alert tuning (actionable):
1) Introduce a dedicated "metric-staleness" alert for each ingestion tier that triggers as a P2 (notify but don't page) with these parameters: evaluation_window=15m, for=10m, notify-channel=#infra-alerts. Rationale: gives time for transient collector restarts without escalating.
2) For SLO-derived alerts: require either (a) metric presence check pass or (b) synthetic heartbeat pass. If presence is missing, mark SLO alert as suppressed and surface a single "SLO-eval-paused:missing-metrics" ticket to SRE dashboard.
3) Add pre-paging grouping rules: collapse identical alerts from >5 routes into an aggregated incident so on-call gets a single page with a short diagnostic script attached.
4) Add cardinality-guard to deploy pipeline: if a canary introduces new label cardinality > threshold (e.g., >100 distinct new label values per minute), block auto-promotion and notify infra. Provide a lightweight script to compute delta in CI from sampled metrics.
5) Instrument a lightweight synthetic sequence per-region (1s cadence checks for key endpoints) and use those as a tie-breaker for SLO evaluation.

Suggested PromQL and alert configs to trial (paste-ready):
- Metric staleness alert (P2, slack-only):
  - expr: (time() - max_over_time(timestamp(up{job=~"collector.*"})[15m])) > 300
  - for: 10m
  - labels: severity=P2, category=ingestion
  - annotations: runbook: "Check collector pods, kafka lag, forwarder logs"

- SLO pause guard (mute derived alert if missing):
  - expr: absent(requests_total{service="hosted"}[10m]) == 1
  - for: 5m
  - action: set alert.label.slo_eval_state = "paused-missing-metric" (note: we cannot set labels from alert; instead send to SRE dashboard automation to open a ticket)

Operational playbook snippet for the on-call (concise):
- If pages > 20 in 10m and many are same-name: assume metric staleness.
  - Run: kubectl -n observability get pod -l app=collector -o wide; check restarts
  - Check kafka consumer lag: kafka-consumer-groups --describe --group prometheus-forwarder
  - If collectors healthy, check remote-write endpoint (nginx logs) for 502/504s.
  - Mute SLO-derived pagers for 20m and create SRE ticket with initial diagnostics.

Post-incident actions (owners / timeline):
- SRE-1423 (Marco Li): implement metric-staleness alert and dashboard by 2025-12-31.
- SRE-1427 (Aisha Patel + infra): proof-of-concept cardinality-guard in deploy CI by 2026-01-21.
- SRE-1435 (Jonas Herrera): synthetic heartbeat rollout for eu-west1 and us-west2 by 2026-02-05.
- Run a 2-week trial where SLO-derived alerts are gated by metric-presence check (owner: Evelyn) starting 2026-01-15.

Notes to self (on-call tips):
- When muting, always paste the short diagnostic snippet used to justify the mute into the alert mute description. This saves follow-up time.
- Use the MUTE playbook channel template so automated auditors can annotate the incident.
- Prioritize getting a collector pod core dump only when we suspect memory corruption — don't request it for transient OOMs without signs.

Open questions / discussion items for next SRE retro:
- What is acceptable delay for SLO-derived alerting when metric presence is intermittent? 5m? 10m? 15m?
- How do we balance immediate paging (fast ops) vs aggregated paging (prevents chaos) for high-volume customer-facing alerts?
- Should we convert some SLO pages to P2 with mandatory automation that creates a ticket and annotates affected customers?

Appendix: useful links and quick commands
- Confluence: Metric ingestion overview -> https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/metric-ingestion-overview
- Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRE-1423 (staleness alert)
- Slack: #oncall, #infra-alerts, #observability
- Quick kubectl: kubectl -n observability logs deploy/collector -c forwarder --since=20m | sed -n '1,200p'
- Kafka lag check: kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka1:9092 --describe --group prometheus-forwarder

If anything in here looks wrong or missing, mark edits inline and ping me (Evelyn) — this doc will become the starting point for a runbook PR.
